_: One decision inside an ordinary game: should Mario press jump right now? The game loop, physics and rendering stay ordinary code; only this question goes through a proven circuit. Bucketing the raw distances into the codes below is the caller's job and is documented in each field's 'raw'. speed has three legal values in two bits: code 3 is illegal and the circuit answers it with review = 1 by construction.
name: mario-jump
scene: A side-scrolling platform game. Mario runs to the right. Falling into a gap or touching an enemy loses a life. A jump from the ground carries Mario forward a fixed distance: 1 tile when stopped, 2 tiles walking, 3 tiles running. He should press jump exactly when a gap or an enemy lies ahead within that distance, so the jump carries him past it; jumping when nothing is within that distance lands him short or wastes the jump. He cannot jump in mid-air.
question: Should Mario press jump at this exact moment?

gap_ahead.raw: tiles from Mario to the next gap, capped at 7; 0 when no gap is in view

values.7: a gap 7 or more tiles ahead

enemy_ahead.raw: tiles from Mario to the next enemy, capped at 7; 0 when no enemy is in view

values.7: an enemy 7 or more tiles ahead

on_ground.raw: 1 when Mario's feet touch a floor tile

values.1: Mario is standing or running on the ground

speed.raw: 0 stopped, 1 walking, 2 running; there is no code 3
